facts.text: Bywater was originally part of Faubourg Washington, a plantation subdivision populated by African Americans, Haitians, and poor European immigrants in early 1800s.
The neighborhood’s name comes from its location on the Mississippi River’s natural levee, downriver from Vieux Carré and Faubourg Marigny.
Bywater hosts the historic marker commemorating Homer Plessy’s 1898 removal from a railroad car, a pivotal moment in the Plessy v. Ferguson case.
The Society of Saint Anne krewe starts its Mardi Gras procession in Bywater each year, gathering marchers before heading through the French Quarter.
After Hurricane Katrina, Bywater’s slightly higher elevation made it one of the first neighborhoods to recover, attracting many survivors.
The Bywater Bone Boys Social Aid and Pleasure Club, founded in 2005, leads a pre‑7 a.m. walking parade of local artists and performers.
